exercise_bank.title: Balloon Breaths
exercise_bank.instructions: Pretend you are blowing up a big balloon. Take a slow deep breath in, then say 'I can speak slowly and clearly' as you let the breath out evenly.
exercise_bank.notes: Pairs breath support with calm paced speech.

exercise_bank.title: Bounce the Ball
exercise_bank.instructions: Say each syllable of these words like you are bouncing a ball: wa-ter-mel-on, but-ter-fly, el-e-phant.
exercise_bank.notes: Builds syllable segmentation awareness useful for stuttering blocks.

exercise_bank.title: Animal Race
exercise_bank.instructions: Say each animal name slowly one syllable at a time like you are walking it across the room: Tor...toise. Tur...key. Pen...guin. Cro...co...dile.
exercise_bank.notes: Builds awareness of slowing down without losing the word.

exercise_bank.title: Clap and Talk
exercise_bank.instructions: Clap once for every word as you say this sentence: I (clap) like (clap) to (clap) play (clap) outside (clap). Try it again a little slower.
exercise_bank.notes: Uses physical rhythm to externally pace speech.

exercise_bank.title: No Um Story
exercise_bank.instructions: Tell me about your favourite game without saying um or uh. If you get stuck just take a breath instead.
exercise_bank.notes: Replaces filler words with a pause habit.

exercise_bank.title: Question Ping Pong
exercise_bank.instructions: I will ask you a question, take a breath before you answer then answer slowly. Ready? What is your favourite colour?
exercise_bank.notes: Builds the breath-before-speaking habit in conversation.

exercise_bank.title: Slow Motion Reader
exercise_bank.instructions: Read this sentence like you are a robot moving in slow motion: The. Big. Dog. Ran. Fast. Now try it at normal speed but still clear.
exercise_bank.notes: Transitions from exaggerated slow pace to natural pace.

exercise_bank.title: Dragon Breaths
exercise_bank.instructions: Take a big breath like a dragon about to breathe fire then say 'I am a strong speaker' slowly as you let it out.
exercise_bank.notes: Fun framing for breath support practice.

exercise_bank.title: Pre-Talk Breath Reset
exercise_bank.instructions: Before answering a question take a slow breath in for 3 seconds and out for 4. Practice this before saying: 'My name is ___ and I am in grade ___.
exercise_bank.notes: Builds the pause-and-breathe habit before speaking in class.

exercise_bank.title: Slow Read Relay
exercise_bank.instructions: Read this sentence at half your normal speed: 'Yesterday I went to school and had a really interesting class about history.' Now try it at normal speed keeping the same clarity.
exercise_bank.notes: Pacing drill using a relatable teen scenario.

exercise_bank.title: No Filler Recap
exercise_bank.instructions: Recap what you did yesterday without using um, uh, like, or you know. If you need a second just pause silently.
exercise_bank.notes: Targets the most common teen filler words in casual speech.

exercise_bank.title: Class Presentation Opener
exercise_bank.instructions: Practice saying the opening line of a school presentation: 'Today I will be talking about...' Keep it smooth and unhurried.
exercise_bank.notes: Targets a high-anxiety real scenario for teens.

exercise_bank.title: Teacher Question Practice
exercise_bank.instructions: Practice answering a teacher-style question calmly: 'Can you explain what you understand about this topic?' Take a breath first then answer slowly.
exercise_bank.notes: Simulates a common in-class anxiety trigger.

exercise_bank.title: Group Chat Out Loud
exercise_bank.instructions: Imagine you are saying your next text message out loud to a group of friends. Speak it naturally at a calm pace without rushing.
exercise_bank.notes: Bridges the gap between texting habits and spoken fluency.

exercise_bank.title: Pause at Punctuation
exercise_bank.instructions: Read this short paragraph aloud pausing visibly at every comma and full stop even if it feels slow: 'Last weekend, I went to the mall with my friends. We had lunch, watched a movie, and walked around for hours.'
exercise_bank.notes: Builds intentional pause control to prevent rushing.

exercise_bank.title: Easy Start
exercise_bank.instructions: Practice starting sentences with a gentle stretched first sound rather than a hard stop. Try: Hhhello instead of a blocked Hello. Iiit was a good day.
exercise_bank.notes: Easy onset technique adapted for a teen-friendly framing.

exercise_bank.title: Paced Paragraph Reading
exercise_bank.instructions: Read this paragraph aloud at a deliberately slow even pace pausing at every comma and period: 'The morning sun rose slowly over the quiet city. People began their day, walking calmly to work, sipping coffee, and greeting neighbors.'
exercise_bank.notes: Tracks words-per-minute as a baseline fluency metric.

exercise_bank.title: Diaphragmatic Breathing Drill
exercise_bank.instructions: Inhale deeply through your nose for 4 seconds, hold for 2, then say a full sentence as you exhale slowly over 6 seconds.
exercise_bank.notes: Builds breath support to reduce rushed speech.

exercise_bank.title: Filler-Free Minute
exercise_bank.instructions: Speak for one minute about your day without using filler words like um, uh, or like. Pause silently instead when you need a moment.
exercise_bank.notes: Direct filler word reduction practice with self-monitoring.

exercise_bank.title: Comma Breathing
exercise_bank.instructions: Read a paragraph aloud taking a visible pause and breath at every comma even if it feels longer than natural.
exercise_bank.notes: Builds intentional pause control to prevent rushing.

exercise_bank.title: Unscripted Topic Talk
exercise_bank.instructions: Talk for 90 seconds about a topic you were not prepared for such as describing your morning routine focusing on staying calm and paced even without a script.
exercise_bank.notes: Tests fluency under spontaneous less controlled conditions.

exercise_bank.title: Easy Onset Practice
exercise_bank.instructions: Practice starting sentences with a gentle stretched first sound rather than a hard stop. For example: Hhhello how are you instead of a blocked H-h-hello.
exercise_bank.notes: Easy onset technique commonly used in stuttering therapy.

exercise_bank.title: Sentence-Per-Breath
exercise_bank.instructions: Say one full short sentence per breath: I am learning to speak smoothly. Pause and take a new breath before the next sentence.
exercise_bank.notes: Prevents running out of air mid-sentence which can cause rushing.

exercise_bank.title: Metronome Reading
exercise_bank.instructions: Read a short paragraph aloud placing equal timing on each word similar to a metronome beat.
exercise_bank.notes: Useful for cluttering or rapid uneven speech rate.

exercise_bank.title: Ship or Sheep
exercise_bank.instructions: Say these word pairs out loud: ship - sheep, chip - cheap, sip - seep. Try to make them sound different from each other.
exercise_bank.notes: Classic minimal pair drill for sound discrimination.

exercise_bank.title: Snake Sounds
exercise_bank.instructions: Make a long snake sound sssssss for 5 seconds then say sun, sand, snake, soup.
exercise_bank.notes: Isolates the S sound before placing it in words.

exercise_bank.title: Red Rabbit Run
exercise_bank.instructions: Say slowly three times: Red rabbit runs around. Then try it a little faster each time.
exercise_bank.notes: Targets the R sound in a playful repeated phrase.

exercise_bank.title: Thumbs Up Thursday
exercise_bank.instructions: Practice the th sound by saying: thumb, think, three, Thursday. Put your tongue gently between your teeth for each one.
exercise_bank.notes: Visual tactile cue helps children locate tongue placement.

exercise_bank.title: Lion or Line
exercise_bank.instructions: Say these pairs: lion - line, light - night, low - flow. Listen for the L sound at the start.
exercise_bank.notes: Reinforces L sound clarity.

exercise_bank.title: Silly Sally
exercise_bank.instructions: Say three times: Silly Sally sells seashells. Go slow first then a little faster.
exercise_bank.notes: Classic twister targeting S sound repetition.

exercise_bank.title: Sound Story
exercise_bank.instructions: Tell a short story using as many words with your practice sound as you can. For example using S words: sun, snake, sandwich, swim.
exercise_bank.notes: Moves target sound from drills into spontaneous speech.

exercise_bank.title: Funny Fox
exercise_bank.instructions: Say each word clearly feeling your top teeth touch your bottom lip: fox, fun, fish, five, village, voice.
exercise_bank.notes: Targets F and V sounds with tactile placement cue.

exercise_bank.title: Think or Sink
exercise_bank.instructions: Say these pairs clearly: think - sink, three - free, thank - sank. Focus on putting your tongue between your teeth for the th sound.
exercise_bank.notes: Targets a sound teens often drop in casual speech.

exercise_bank.title: Really Clearly
exercise_bank.instructions: Say three times at increasing speed: Really red lorries rolled down really long roads.
exercise_bank.notes: Targets R and L in a teen-appropriate challenge format.

exercise_bank.title: Text to Talk
exercise_bank.instructions: Say this out loud as clearly as you would type it in a message: I am on my way, be there in five minutes. No mumbling or dropping sounds.
exercise_bank.notes: Bridges teen texting habits with spoken articulation.

exercise_bank.title: Sentence Final S
exercise_bank.instructions: Say these sentences clearly emphasizing the final S sound: The cats chase the rats. She wears dresses to classes.
exercise_bank.notes: Targets a commonly dropped sound in connected teen speech.

exercise_bank.title: Read It Right
exercise_bank.instructions: Read this paragraph aloud clearly making sure every word ending is fully pronounced: 'Last night I finished my homework, watched a film, and talked to my friends for a bit.'
exercise_bank.notes: Targets word-ending clarity in connected natural speech.

exercise_bank.title: Very or Wary
exercise_bank.instructions: Say these pairs clearly: very - wary, vine - wine, vest - west.
exercise_bank.notes: V vs W distinction common challenge for several language backgrounds.

exercise_bank.title: Group Intro
exercise_bank.instructions: Introduce yourself to an imaginary new group at school. Say your name, grade, and one hobby clearly and confidently.
exercise_bank.notes: Practices articulation in a socially relevant teen scenario.

exercise_bank.title: Six Slippery Snails
exercise_bank.instructions: Say three times: Six slippery snails slid slowly seaward. Go slow then speed up carefully.
exercise_bank.notes: Fun S-focused tongue twister appropriate for teens.

exercise_bank.title: R vs L Pair Drill
exercise_bank.instructions: Say these word pairs clearly: right - light, road - load, rip - lip, correct - collect.
exercise_bank.notes: Common difficulty area especially for L1 interference.

exercise_bank.title: Thirty Three Thieves
exercise_bank.instructions: Say three times at increasing speed: Thirty-three thieves thought they thrilled the throne throughout Thursday.
exercise_bank.notes: Dense TH sound repetition for adult-level challenge.

exercise_bank.title: Sentence Final S
exercise_bank.instructions: Say these sentences clearly emphasizing the final S sound: The cats chase the rats. She sells dresses.
exercise_bank.notes: Targets a commonly dropped sound in connected speech.

exercise_bank.title: Very Well
exercise_bank.instructions: Say these pairs clearly: very - wary, vine - wine, vest - west.
exercise_bank.notes: Common confusion pair for several language backgrounds.

exercise_bank.title: Target Sound Paragraph
exercise_bank.instructions: Read a short paragraph aloud that contains many instances of your target sound focusing on clear production throughout.
exercise_bank.notes: Moves drilled sound into connected natural speech.

exercise_bank.title: Clear and Quick
exercise_bank.instructions: Describe your weekend plans in under 30 seconds while keeping every word fully clear not rushed or mumbled.
exercise_bank.notes: Tests articulation clarity at natural conversational speed.

exercise_bank.title: Peter Piper Advanced
exercise_bank.instructions: Say three times at increasing speed: Peter Piper picked a peck of pickled peppers. Focus on every P being crisp and clear.
exercise_bank.notes: Multi-sound adult-level articulation challenge.

exercise_bank.title: F and V Contrast
exercise_bank.instructions: Say clearly feeling your top teeth on your bottom lip: fan - van, feel - veal, fast - vast, fine - vine.
exercise_bank.notes: F vs V contrast drill for adult learners.

exercise_bank.title: Short or Long
exercise_bank.instructions: Say these word pairs clearly: pin - pen, ship - sheep, bit - beat. Try to make them sound different.
exercise_bank.notes: Simplified vowel pair practice for younger learners.

exercise_bank.title: Clap the Beat
exercise_bank.instructions: Clap on the strong part of the word: BUT-ter-fly, EL-e-phant, BAS-ket-ball.
exercise_bank.notes: Uses clapping to teach syllable stress in a playful way.

exercise_bank.title: Crisp Sounds
exercise_bank.instructions: Say these words slowly making sure every sound is clear: cat, dog, top, big, map.
exercise_bank.notes: Builds general sound crispness for younger non-native speakers.

exercise_bank.title: Simple Sentence Reading
exercise_bank.instructions: Read this sentence slowly and clearly: The little cat sat on the red mat.
exercise_bank.notes: Short simple passage suitable as a baseline for younger learners.

exercise_bank.title: Happy or Sad Voice
exercise_bank.instructions: Say 'I like pizza' in a happy voice then in a sad voice. Notice how your voice goes up and down differently.
exercise_bank.notes: Introduces intonation awareness through emotion-based contrast.

exercise_bank.title: Vowel Zoo
exercise_bank.instructions: Say each vowel sound with an animal: A as in cat, E as in elephant, I as in iguana, O as in octopus, U as in umbrella bird.
exercise_bank.notes: Makes vowel sounds memorable through association.

exercise_bank.title: Smooth Talker
exercise_bank.instructions: Say this phrase as one smooth flow without stopping between words: I want to go to the park. Notice how the words connect together.
exercise_bank.notes: Introduces connected speech in a child-friendly context.

exercise_bank.title: Question or Statement
exercise_bank.instructions: Say 'You like ice cream' as a statement then as a question. Notice your voice goes up at the end for the question.
exercise_bank.notes: Builds intonation awareness for question vs statement patterns.

exercise_bank.title: Stress Shift Challenge
exercise_bank.instructions: Say these noun and verb pairs noticing the stress shift: RE-cord vs re-CORD, PRE-sent vs pre-SENT, OB-ject vs ob-JECT.
exercise_bank.notes: Stress placement can change meaning in English, highly relevant for teen learners.

exercise_bank.title: Vowel Contrast Drill
exercise_bank.instructions: Say these pairs clearly: ship - sheep, bit - beat, full - fool, bed - bad.
exercise_bank.notes: Vowel length and quality distinctions common in second language speakers.

exercise_bank.title: Natural Linking
exercise_bank.instructions: Practice saying these phrases as one smooth connected sound: turn it off, kind of, I don't know. Notice how native speakers link sounds.
exercise_bank.notes: Connected speech is key to sounding natural in casual teen conversation.

exercise_bank.title: Paragraph Clarity
exercise_bank.instructions: Read this sentence clearly at natural speed: 'Yesterday I finished my homework early and went out with my friends to grab some food.'
exercise_bank.notes: Everyday teen scenario used as pronunciation baseline.

exercise_bank.title: Emphasis Changes Meaning
exercise_bank.instructions: Say this sentence four times stressing a different word each time: I never said she took it. Notice how the meaning changes each time.
exercise_bank.notes: Advanced intonation drill showing how stress changes interpretation.

exercise_bank.title: Cluster Practice
exercise_bank.instructions: Practice these consonant clusters slowly: str in street, spl in splash, thr in three, str in strong.
exercise_bank.notes: Consonant clusters are difficult for many language backgrounds.

exercise_bank.title: Explain It To Me
exercise_bank.instructions: Explain how to play your favourite game or sport to someone who has never heard of it. Speak clearly and at a natural pace.
exercise_bank.notes: Uses a relatable teen context to practice pronunciation in spontaneous speech.

exercise_bank.title: Read With Feeling
exercise_bank.instructions: Read this sentence with natural rise and fall in your voice: 'I honestly cannot believe that happened. That is the most surprising thing I have heard all week.'
exercise_bank.notes: Builds natural intonation in extended speech.

exercise_bank.title: Stress the Right Syllable
exercise_bank.instructions: Say these words placing stress on the correct syllable: PHO-to-graph, pho-TOG-ra-pher, pho-to-GRAPH-ic.
exercise_bank.notes: Word stress shifts are a common second-language challenge.

exercise_bank.title: Short and Long Vowels
exercise_bank.instructions: Say these pairs clearly: ship - sheep, bit - beat, full - fool.
exercise_bank.notes: Vowel length distinctions vary widely across languages.

exercise_bank.title: Question vs Statement Tone
exercise_bank.instructions: Say 'You are coming today' as a statement then as a question noticing how your pitch rises at the end.
exercise_bank.notes: Builds awareness of intonation patterns that affect meaning.

exercise_bank.title: Cluster Practice
exercise_bank.instructions: Practice these consonant clusters slowly: str in street, spl in splash, thr in three.
exercise_bank.notes: Consonant clusters are difficult for many language backgrounds.

exercise_bank.title: Natural Linking
exercise_bank.instructions: Practice saying these as one smooth phrase: turn it off, kind of, I do not know. Notice how native speakers link sounds together.
exercise_bank.notes: Connected speech and linking are key to natural-sounding fluency.

exercise_bank.title: Baseline Clarity Passage
exercise_bank.instructions: Read this passage aloud at natural pace focusing on clear vowel and consonant sounds: 'Yesterday I walked to the store and bought some fresh bread and vegetables.'
exercise_bank.notes: General clarity passage useful as a baseline recording.

exercise_bank.title: Emphasis Changes Meaning
exercise_bank.instructions: Say this sentence four times stressing a different word each time: I never said she took it.
exercise_bank.notes: Stress placement can change interpretation entirely.

exercise_bank.title: Noun Verb Stress Pairs
exercise_bank.instructions: Say these noun and verb pairs noticing the stress shift: RE-cord vs re-CORD, PRE-sent vs pre-SENT.
exercise_bank.notes: Common stress pair confusion for adult learners.

exercise_bank.title: Show and Tell
exercise_bank.instructions: Pick your favourite toy or object and tell me three things about it. Take your time there is no rush.
exercise_bank.notes: Low pressure storytelling builds comfort speaking about familiar topics.

exercise_bank.title: Picture Detective
exercise_bank.instructions: Look at something around you right now and tell me everything you can see like you are a detective finding clues.
exercise_bank.notes: Removes social pressure by framing speech as a game.

exercise_bank.title: Pretend Phone Call
exercise_bank.instructions: Pretend you are calling a friend to invite them to your birthday party. What would you say?
exercise_bank.notes: Practices a real-life social speaking scenario safely.

exercise_bank.title: Quick Questions
exercise_bank.instructions: I will ask you easy questions and you answer in a full sentence. What is your favourite food? What do you like to do after school?
exercise_bank.notes: Builds comfort answering questions without long pauses.

exercise_bank.title: My Best Day Ever
exercise_bank.instructions: Tell me a story about the best day you ever had. Try to talk for at least one minute.
exercise_bank.notes: Encourages sustained spontaneous speech with positive framing.

exercise_bank.title: Order at a Restaurant
exercise_bank.instructions: Pretend you are ordering your favourite food at a restaurant. What do you say to the waiter?
exercise_bank.notes: Low stakes real-world scenario children can relate to.

exercise_bank.title: Make Up a Story
exercise_bank.instructions: Make up a story about a superhero. Tell me who they are, what their power is, and what happened today.
exercise_bank.notes: Creative framing reduces self-consciousness in extended speech.

exercise_bank.title: Favourite Things
exercise_bank.instructions: Answer in full sentences: What is your favourite movie and why? What is something you are really good at?
exercise_bank.notes: Positive topic builds confidence and reduces speaking anxiety.

exercise_bank.title: Describe Your Space
exercise_bank.instructions: Look around your room or wherever you are and describe what you see for 30 seconds. No script needed just talk.
exercise_bank.notes: Low stakes warmup that removes the pressure of a topic.

exercise_bank.title: Talking to a Teacher
exercise_bank.instructions: Practice asking your teacher to explain something you did not understand: 'Excuse me, I had a question about the homework. Could you explain...'
exercise_bank.notes: Targets a common anxiety-inducing scenario for teens.

exercise_bank.title: Hot Seat Questions
exercise_bank.instructions: Answer in full confident sentences: What are you proud of this year? What is something you wish more people knew about you?
exercise_bank.notes: Positive introspective topics build confidence without high stakes.

exercise_bank.title: Tell Me About Something You Love
exercise_bank.instructions: Talk for 60 seconds about a game, show, sport, or hobby you love. Pretend you are recommending it to a friend.
exercise_bank.notes: Relatable topic removes the blank-mind anxiety of unfamiliar subjects.

exercise_bank.title: Class Presentation Practice
exercise_bank.instructions: Deliver the opening 30 seconds of an imaginary school presentation on any topic you choose. Speak like you mean it.
exercise_bank.notes: Simulates the highest anxiety speaking scenario for most teens.

exercise_bank.title: Small Talk Warmup
exercise_bank.instructions: Practice answering naturally: How was your weekend? What have you been up to lately?
exercise_bank.notes: Targets everyday casual conversation teens often avoid.

exercise_bank.title: Unprepared Opinion
exercise_bank.instructions: Give your honest opinion on this topic for 60 seconds without preparing: Should school start later in the morning?
exercise_bank.notes: Builds spontaneous speaking confidence on a teen-relevant debate topic.

exercise_bank.title: Saying No Confidently
exercise_bank.instructions: Practice saying no politely but clearly: Your friend asks you to do something you do not want to do. What do you say?
exercise_bank.notes: Builds assertive speaking skills in a relatable teen context.

exercise_bank.title: Describe What You See
exercise_bank.instructions: Describe a photo or scene around you for 30 seconds without overthinking your wording.
exercise_bank.notes: Low-stakes warmup for spontaneous speaking.

exercise_bank.title: Mock Interview Question
exercise_bank.instructions: Answer this as if in a job interview: Tell me about yourself. Aim for 60 to 90 seconds.
exercise_bank.notes: Targets a high-anxiety real-world speaking scenario.

exercise_bank.title: Asking for Something
exercise_bank.instructions: Practice asking a coworker for help with a task speaking clearly and directly without over-apologizing.
exercise_bank.notes: Builds assertiveness in professional speaking contexts.

exercise_bank.title: Unprepared Topic Talk
exercise_bank.instructions: Speak for two minutes about a skill you would like to learn without preparing in advance.
exercise_bank.notes: Builds tolerance for speaking without a script.

exercise_bank.title: Small Talk Starters
exercise_bank.instructions: Practice answering naturally: How was your weekend? and What do you do for work?
exercise_bank.notes: Targets everyday social speaking situations.

exercise_bank.title: 30 Second Pitch
exercise_bank.instructions: Imagine introducing yourself to a room of new colleagues. Give a brief confident 30 second introduction.
exercise_bank.notes: Simulates public speaking pressure in a controlled way.

exercise_bank.title: Difficult Question Practice
exercise_bank.instructions: Answer this directly and confidently: What is your greatest weakness? Take a breath first then respond.
exercise_bank.notes: Targets a common high-anxiety question in professional settings.

exercise_bank.title: Tell Me Something Good
exercise_bank.instructions: Tell me about something positive that happened to you recently. Take your time and speak naturally.
exercise_bank.notes: Positive framing reduces speaking anxiety for a warmup session.

exercise_bank.title: Practice Mix-Up
exercise_bank.instructions: Let us do a little bit of everything today. One slow sentence, one tongue twister, and one short story about your day.
exercise_bank.notes: Light combined session for kids maintaining therapy progress.

exercise_bank.title: Tell Me About Today
exercise_bank.instructions: Tell me one good thing and one tricky thing about your day.
exercise_bank.notes: Simple low-pressure daily check-in for younger users.

exercise_bank.title: Practice Recap
exercise_bank.instructions: Show me your best sentence from today. The one you are most proud of saying clearly.
exercise_bank.notes: Builds positive reinforcement into the maintenance routine.

exercise_bank.title: Weekend Story
exercise_bank.instructions: Tell me what you did last weekend in three sentences. Take your time.
exercise_bank.notes: Familiar topic lowers pressure while maintaining speaking practice.

exercise_bank.title: What Was Hard Today
exercise_bank.instructions: Tell me one thing about speaking that felt hard today and one thing that felt easy.
exercise_bank.notes: Builds self-monitoring awareness in younger users.

exercise_bank.title: Weekly Check-In
exercise_bank.instructions: Tell me how your speaking has felt this week. Any moments where you felt more confident or more stuck than usual?
exercise_bank.notes: Combines reflection with fluency and confidence practice.

exercise_bank.title: Open Chat
exercise_bank.instructions: Just talk to me about anything on your mind today. No topic required.
exercise_bank.notes: Low-structure session to maintain natural speaking habits.

exercise_bank.title: Read and Reflect
exercise_bank.instructions: Read a short paragraph from anything you like, a book, article, or even a social media post, then tell me one thing you noticed about how you spoke.
exercise_bank.notes: Self-monitoring through reading in a teen-relevant format.

exercise_bank.title: Real Life Replay
exercise_bank.instructions: Think of a conversation you had today that felt challenging. Replay it now but this time speak the way you wish you had.
exercise_bank.notes: Encourages transfer of skills to real-world situations.

exercise_bank.title: What Clicked Today
exercise_bank.instructions: Tell me one speaking strategy you used today and whether it helped.
exercise_bank.notes: Reinforces strategy use and builds self-awareness.

exercise_bank.title: Daily Check-In
exercise_bank.instructions: Talk for one minute about how your speech practice has felt this week. Notice anything that has improved.
exercise_bank.notes: Combines reflection with fluency and confidence practice.

exercise_bank.title: Mixed Skills Passage
exercise_bank.instructions: Read a short paragraph aloud paying attention to pacing, clarity, and pausing all at once.
exercise_bank.notes: Combined practice reinforcing multiple skills together.

exercise_bank.title: Open Conversation
exercise_bank.instructions: Have an open free-flowing conversation about anything on your mind today.
exercise_bank.notes: Low-structure session to maintain natural speaking habits.

exercise_bank.title: Progress Journal
exercise_bank.instructions: Record yourself describing one thing you noticed about your speech this week, good or challenging.
exercise_bank.notes: Builds self-awareness and ties into the progress dashboard.

exercise_bank.title: Therapist Style Check-In
exercise_bank.instructions: Answer as if your therapist asked: What is one strategy you used this week and how did it go?
exercise_bank.notes: Mirrors language used in real therapy sessions for continuity.
